modes: st: StIdle, StMsgFeed, StProcessing, StAbsorbed, StSqueezing, StTerminalError
sw_cmd_i: CmdNone, CmdStart, CmdProcess, CmdManualRun, CmdDone

guarantees.claim: When st is StTerminalError, sparse_fsm_error_o is set to 1 and err_swsequence is set to 0, regardless of sw_cmd_i.
When st does not match any explicit case item, sparse_fsm_error_o is set to 1 and err_swsequence is set to 0.
guarantees.cond: st not in {StIdle, StMsgFeed, StProcessing, StAbsorbed, StSqueezing, StTerminalError}

guarantees.claim: When st is StIdle, err_swsequence is asserted if sw_cmd_i is not CmdNone or CmdStart.
When st is StMsgFeed, err_swsequence is asserted if sw_cmd_i is not CmdNone or CmdProcess.
When st is StProcessing or StSqueezing, err_swsequence is asserted if sw_cmd_i is not equal to CmdNone.
When st is StAbsorbed, err_swsequence is asserted if sw_cmd_i is not CmdNone, CmdManualRun, or CmdDone.
When st is StIdle, StMsgFeed, StProcessing, StAbsorbed, or StSqueezing, sparse_fsm_error_o remains 0.
guarantees.cond: st in {StIdle, StMsgFeed, StProcessing, StAbsorbed, StSqueezing}

assumptions.claim: sw_cmd_i is a stable, valid encoded command value and st is a stable, valid state encoding (non-meta-stable, non-X) so that the unique case and inside operator behave deterministically.
assumptions.risk: Meta-stability or X on st or sw_cmd_i can cause glitches on err_swsequence and sparse_fsm_error_o, leading to false error assertions or masked real errors.

assumptions.claim: The logic receiving err_swsequence must use it to block the execution of the corresponding command when asserted.
assumptions.risk: If downstream ignores err_swsequence, a disallowed command will be executed, violating the state-dependent command protocol and potentially leading to data corruption or security breach.

uncertain_points.claim: In StTerminalError state, err_swsequence is forced to 0, masking any disallowed command that might be asserted. The design relies solely on sparse_fsm_error_o to contain faults, but if the command interface remains active, an illegal command could be processed.
uncertain_points.cond: st == StTerminalError and sw_cmd_i is disallowed
uncertain_points.risk: A dangerous command could be accepted despite the terminal error if downstream logic does not adequately act on sparse_fsm_error_o.

uncertain_points.claim: In the default case (unrecognized state), err_swsequence is forced to 0. An attacker or fault that forces an illegal state can then issue a dangerous command without being flagged as a sequence error.
uncertain_points.risk: An illegal command could be executed because err_swsequence remains 0, bypassing command checking if the system only uses err_swsequence to gate commands.

uncertain_points.claim: The effectiveness of sparse_fsm_error_o depends entirely on the system-level response; local RTL does not enforce that st stops updating or that commands are blocked when sparse_fsm_error_o is high.
uncertain_points.risk: If st continues to change, err_swsequence could return to 0 prematurely or the design could exit the error state, undermining fault containment.
